title: FreeCAD subprocess and support-boundary refresh
mode: primary-source web research and read-only local source/test audit
scope: Trace current FreeCAD DWG-to-DXF subprocess invocation and success condition
Reconcile the standard FreeCAD importer scope for ACIS/AcDs modeler carriers
Compare FreeCAD argv with the local dwg2dxf CLI and existing fast/optional controls
Refine native acceptance criteria without expanding routine validation

method.kind: Inspect current FreeCAD source and official documentation, then audit the matching local CLI and tests
method.limitations: The source/documentation review is not a runtime qualification of any FreeCAD build, OS, converter binary, DXF importer backend, add-on, or ACIS payload. No support claim follows from documentation alone.

sources.revision: mutable main source accessed 2026-10-18; converter path around lines 1500-1558
sources.observed: The LibreDWG branch creates a temporary directory and invokes dwg2dxf with [input, '-o', output]. After Popen.communicate(), the wrapper returns the result when the path exists; it does not visibly test the child return code in this path. This describes the wrapper, not a libdxfrw defect.

The documented standard route uses an external DWG converter followed by the selected DXF importer, so importer limitations apply. The format overview describes stock DXF/standard DWG conversion as 2D-only for proprietary ACIS content; CADExchanger is documented as a separate 3D DWG route. Documentation is scope evidence, not runtime or solid-semantic qualification.

The CLI implements the same input/-o/output contract and a dedicated fast FreeCAD compatibility check exists. An optional real-wrapper failure-path test asserts that a failed conversion does not hand off a partial DXF. These local controls do not substitute for Linux/Windows FreeCAD runtime results.

assessment.planImpact: Native acceptance must check process status, fresh output identity, parse/readback, and the expected manifest independently of FreeCAD's output-exists wrapper condition. Preserve stock FreeCAD as a 2D/explicit-entity lane and keep ACIS/AcDs semantic evidence in a separately qualified modeler-capable route. Reuse existing fast and optional test owners; no duplicate validation is needed.

implementationReadyChecks: Keep the fast FreeCAD argv/CLI contract as the routine check; do not start FreeCAD for each local slice.

At native Linux and Windows checkpoints, run the installed converter in a unique fresh temporary directory and independently require a zero return code, a fresh output, successful DXF parse/readback, and identity-level expected dispositions.
Record the exact FreeCAD build, converter path/version/hash, argv, requested and actual DXF revision/hash, importer backend, preferences, output status, and diagnostics.
Treat stock FreeCAD ACIS/AcDs solid semantics as outside the documented stock importer scope; carrier bytes and entity shells do not establish a valid body.
Use a named, pinned modeler-capable reader for B-rep validity/measurements and separately verify the DWG AcDs owner/key/prototype/history graph.
Keep all native checks optional and at the composed checkpoint; if a route or artifact is unavailable, report that evidence cell as NOT_RUN or NOT_QUALIFIED and continue local implementation.
